Join us as a Customer Due Diligence Analyst, Onboarding at Mettle


  • If you have a curious mind and like to work in a fast paced, innovative environment, this is a fantastic opportunity to join us as a Customer Due Diligence Analyst.
  • You’ll work diligently and efficiently to protect our customers and the organisation from economic crime
  • This is an opportunity to join a supportive team where we’ll also take a real investment in your career development

What you'll do


In this role within the Customer Due Diligence function, you will primarily focus on the Mettle proposition, supporting Boxed banking-as-a-service processes as needed. As a key part of our first line of defence against economic crime, you will ensure regulatory obligations are met, conduct efficient account reviews, and risk assess customers using various sources to confirm they meet our risk appetite.


You’ll be responsible for:


  • Conducting robust reviews of new Mettle account applications, ensuring our customers align with NatWest Boxed's risk appetite. You'll make fair and proportionate decline decisions where required
  • Identifying and mitigating economic crime risks, escalating effectively when needed to protect both our customers and Mettle
  • Operating diligently within NatWest Group policies and NatWest Boxed established processes, ensuring compliance and consistency
  • Constantly seeking opportunities to enhance our processes for greater effectiveness and efficiency, helping us scale and improve
  • Reviewing Know Your Customer (KYC) / Know Your Business (KYB) check reports and application data to prevent application fraud and truly understand the nature and purpose of the account
  • Reviewing name screening hits for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), Sanctions, and Adverse Press. This involves escalating true matches or making well-rationalised discounting decisions
  • Investigating application fraud and other economic crime-related alerts from internal and external databases, like the Untoward Incident Database (UID) and Cifas
  • Contacting customers, managing your chats within our Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and communicating clearly and concisely, always embodying Mettle's supportive tone of voice

The skills you'll need


Seeking a curious and innovative individual with CDD or Financial Crime knowledge. Recognised qualifications are helpful but not necessary - we can help you achieve these once you join. Strong communication skills and a focus on positive customer outcomes are essential.


You’ll also need:

  • Previous experience in customer due diligence, economic crime prevention, or similar fields (e.g. AML, PEPs/Sanctions, KYC/KYB).
  • A curious and analytical mind, adept at applying a risk-based approach to efficiently manage high volumes of work.
  • Proven ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, handling multiple priorities with precision and calm.
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with a strong command of English.
  • Sharp critical thinking, sound decision-making, and exceptional time management.
  • Meticulous attention to detail and a proactive, self-starting approach to your work and record-keeping.

Our Company

PharMerica

Overview

Step Into a Rewarding Role as a Claims Specialist with PharMerica!

Are you ready to make a real impact in a growing organization? Join our PharMerica team as a Claims Specialist, where you'll play a key role in ensuring our long-term care and senior living clients receive the pharmaceutical support they need. We offer a non-retail, closed-door pharmacy environment, allowing you to focus on what truly matters—delivering exceptional care and service.

Why Join PharMerica?

  • Focused on Service Excellence: Our mission is to provide top-quality care and outstanding customer service to hospitals, rehabilitation centers, long-term acute care hospitals, and specialized care centers across the nation.
  • Career Growth: We’re in high growth mode, offering plenty of opportunities for those looking to advance their careers.

What You’ll Do: As a dynamic Claims Specialist, you will:

raw.description:
The Team Lead - Acute Billing Operations is responsible for day‑to‑day operational performance and execution for assigned clients, serving as the primary operations liaison between client facilities and internal delivery teams. This role focuses on tactical revenue cycle outcomes, ensuring accurate reporting, effective communication, and consistent execution across full-cycle claims processing. (billing, follow‑up, collections, denials, and claim resolution workflows)


This position is accountable for operational monitoring and client relationship management. The Team Lead translates client needs into clear operational priorities, monitors key performance indicators, identifies risks and trends, and supports timely issue resolution to protect cash, A/R performance, and client satisfaction.


The role also provides operational mentorship to staff by reinforcing daily best practices, supporting training and performance efforts, and helping remove execution barriers. Success is measured by client retention, escalation volume, and core revenue cycle performance indicators.


These Goals and objectives are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed; employees will be required to perform other job-related duties as required. Goals and objectives are subject to change.


All activities must be in compliance with Equal Employment Opportunity laws, HIPAA, ERISA and other regulations, as appropriate.


Essential Functions: In addition to meeting performance expectations, this role includes the following specific responsibilities:


Discrete Responsibilities (Primary Accountability)

  • Operational Performance Monitoring: Monitor daily operational performance, battle cards, action plans, and key KPIs for assigned clients, including A/R days, cash performance, denial trends, and accuracy measures.
  • Primary Operations Liaison: Act as the primary operational point of contact between clients and internal delivery teams, ensuring timely, accurate, and consistent communication.
  • Operational Translation: Translate client needs, issues, and requests into actionable operational priorities and execution plans.
  • Risk & Trend Identification: Identify operational risks, analyze performance trends, and support issue resolution to prevent revenue leakage and service disruption.
  • Reporting & Communication: Ensure accurate reporting, clear status updates, and effective issue communication to internal stakeholders and, as appropriate, client contacts.
  • Client Scope: Lead operational work for domestic‑only clients as needed.

Reporting, Trend Monitoring & Continuous Improvement

  • Trend Monitoring & Corrective Action: Review statistical reports and dashboards to identify operational trends, risks, and deficiencies; develop and implement corrective action plans to improve timeliness, quality, and outcomes.
  • Operational Efficiency: Lead tactical efforts to maximize operational efficiency and optimize reimbursement through standardized workflows, issue triage, and collaboration with cross-functional partners.

Client & Stakeholder Relationship Management (Tactical)

  • Liaison & Communication: Act as the primary operational point of contact between facility management and internal teams, ensuring smooth, timely communication and resolution of day-to-day issues.
  • Service Responsiveness & Escalation: Ensure client inquiries are addressed promptly (including providing timelines to resolution), and proactively escalate risks such as unbilled accounts, claim issues, and operational blockers to leadership.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Partner with internal teams (e.g., operations, finance, payer relations, technology, and strategic client management/sales counterparts) to drive resolution and maintain a consistent client experience.
  • Contract Awareness & Compliance: Understand contract terms and ensure operational billing, invoicing, and service delivery remain within negotiated requirements.

Compliance & Professional Standards

  • Regulatory Knowledge: Maintain current knowledge of hospital billing systems, government payer programs, third-party reimbursement policies, and applicable federal/state regulations.
  • Confidentiality: Maintain confidentiality of patient and client information without exception.
  • Continuous Learning & Industry Awareness: Attend required meetings and remain current on industry trends, legislative changes, and best practices.
  • Customer Invoicing & Accuracy: Ensure accuracy of customer invoices and support monthly invoicing processes as required; validate supporting detail and address discrepancies.
  • Management Expectations / Additional Duties: Perform all functions in alignment with management expectations and complete other duties as assigned.

Key Measures of Success

  • Client Retention and Stability
  • Reduction in Client Escalations
  • Cash Performance vs. Goal
  • A/R Days and Denial Trends

Staff Management

Responsible for ensuring area of responsibility has the talent and resources to meet short- and long-term organizational goals as well as ensuring maximum productivity and performance. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Proactively recruit, screen, and select candidates for current and future resource requirements.
  • Effectively orient new hires to ensure a positive and productive employee engagement experience.
  • Ensure structure and hiring plans (within budget) are appropriate for performance and productivity levels required.
  • Utilize the company’s performance management program as designed to align individual performance to overall performance objectives. Meet all completion requirements at a high quality level. Provide ongoing performance feedback. Identify and take appropriate action for non-performance.
  • Ensure each employee has a yearly performance review that is reviewed with employee and the review to be sent to Human Resources each year.
  • Ensure each employee has a clear and thorough understanding of their role and responsibilities. Keep job descriptions current for each position.
  • Actively support and participate in organizational development and training programs. Meet all completion requirements at a high quality level.
  • Mentor, guide, and coach direct reports in order to expand their capabilities and performance.
  • Communicate all corporate matters in a positive and timely manner as directed by Corporate Communications or senior managements.
  • Administer all internal policies and procedures in accordance with corporate, human resources, budgetary, and finance guidelines. Ensure accuracy of staff data records.
  • Comply with all employment laws and regulations including, but not limited to, equal employment opportunities for all.

Minimum Requirements:

Education/Experience/Certification Requirements

  • Experience leading/managing a team of 5-10 direct reports (Claims Billers)
  • 5+ years of experience in Acute hospital revenue cycle functions with strong exposure to FULL-CYCLE billing and follow-up/collections and claim resolution.
  • Working knowledge of insurance regulations, reimbursement practices, procedure and diagnosis coding, and automated billing workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to work issues to resolution, including complex account research, root cause identification, and corrective actions.
  • Strong client-facing communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to explain operational findings, timelines, and next steps clearly.
  • Excellent critical thinking, organizational, and time-management skills with strong attention to detail, accuracy, and follow-through.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, Outlook, Word) and comfort working across multiple systems and reporting outputs.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience (to support internal flexibility for hiring and promotion).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2+ years Medicare hospital billing experience and/or demonstrated expertise with government payers (Medicare/Medicaid).
  • Experience supporting hospital billing platforms and/or EHR/RCM systems (e.g., Thrive, Epic, Cerner, or comparable tools).
  • Advanced revenue cycle analytics capability (e.g., trending denials/underpayments, operational KPI reporting, dashboard interpretation).
  • Prior experience in a role requiring client management, escalations, service recovery, and cross-functional coordination.
  • Exposure to invoicing processes, contract compliance validation, and operational performance governance.

raw.description:
We believe in bold ideas, diverse perspectives, and the drive to transform knowledge into impact. Here, your curiosity fuels progress, your voice shapes innovation, and your ambition helps redefine what’s possible within science and learning. We are a culture that obsesses over impact, challenges, and drives what’s next to power infinite possibilities for our customers, colleagues and society at large.

About the Role:

Wiley Research is executing a three-year transformation, from a strong publishing foundation, through a connected intelligence layer, to an essential research infrastructure. AI runs through every stage. The value comes when more than 1,500 Research colleagues use it well in their daily work, and when teams are ready to adopt the agents and workflows Wiley builds.


The Senior Manager, AI Training & Enablement leads AI adoption across Research. The role has two focus areas: (1) moving colleagues toward everyday use of Copilot and Claude, and (2) deepening adoption of agents and AI-enabled workflows in the teams ready for them. With a population this size, focus is central to the job. The role chooses where to invest, builds simple and repeatable plans, and extends its reach through managers and peer champions.


The role works closely with the AI Center of Excellence, which owns governance, controls, and the building of agents, and with the BM&SP crew team, which experiments with operational solutions enabled by AI. It does not set AI policy, approve tools, or build agents. It makes sure colleagues know what is available and permitted, how to use it in their own work, and what is changing in how their team operates.

The role is hands-on: it designs and produces the learning materials and leads live sessions directly, concentrating that effort on priority segments. Materials are deliberately light: one-page role-based starter guides, short live and recorded sessions, example prompts and workflows, and manager talking points. Full curricula are not expected.

This role will evolve as Research evolves. Wiley is in the middle of a transformation, so the scope and priorities described here will be further defined with the VP once the person starts, and will keep changing as the organization does. The right person is flexible and comfortable adjusting course.


Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities below describe what this role may take on. They are possibilities rather than a fixed list. We will confirm scope and sequencing with the person in the role, and refine them as we go, as the organization and the transformation evolve.

1. Adoption Strategy & Prioritization

  • Build and maintain a Research adoption plan: role-family segments, target use cases, sequencing of waves, and success measures. Review it with the VP each quarter.
  • Apply clear prioritization criteria, such as volume of repeatable work, leader sponsorship, team readiness, and availability of proven use cases. State plainly what is deferred and why.
  • Establish baseline usage with data from the AI Center of Excellence and tool reporting, and define a short set of adoption measures.
  • Keep the plan aligned with Research strategic priorities and with the operating rhythm run by BM&SP.

2. Learning Design & Content Development

  • Define learning objectives and key learning points for each priority audience with Research leaders and subject-matter experts, so every asset targets a specific use case and behavior.
  • Develop short, practical materials in plain language that make AI tools and workflows simple: one-page guides, example prompts and workflows, recorded demos and short videos, and micro-learning modules where useful. Use Wiley templates and standards.
  • Extract core information from AI Center of Excellence guidance, existing procedures, subject-matter experts, and crew team pilots, and turn it into role-ready material.
  • Pilot materials with a small group and obtain the needed approvals, including AI Center of Excellence review of policy content, before release.
  • Design for accessibility and varied learning styles, including assistive technologies.
  • Research learner and business needs for each audience, and refine materials from feedback. Keep content current as tools, features, and guardrails change, and retire what is out of date.

3. Everyday Adoption of Copilot and Claude

  • Build role-based starter plans for each priority role family: top use cases, example prompts, short sessions, and office hours.
  • Schedule, coordinate, and deliver short live and virtual sessions and office hours, timed to tool rollouts and key points in the Research calendar.
  • Track training requests, attendance, and completion, and use the data to decide what to build, adjust, or retire next.
  • Build and support a network of peer champions across Research teams, with a light toolkit and regular check-ins. Coach champions and any colleagues supporting this work on content and delivery standards.
  • Equip people managers with talking points and small team activities so adoption continues after launch.
  • Translate guardrails from the AI Center of Excellence into plain-language guidance colleagues can follow in their daily work.
  • Collect questions and barriers from colleagues. Resolve what content can fix and escalate the rest to the AI Center of Excellence.

4. Advanced Adoption of Agents and AI-Enabled Workflows

  • Identify teams ready to move from individual use to shared agents and redesigned workflows, and sequence that work with the AI Center of Excellence and the crew team.
  • Prepare receiving teams for new agents and workflows with quick-start materials and hands-on walkthroughs: what changes, who does what, how to escalate issues, and how success will be measured.
  • Turn proven crew team pilots into short, repeatable guides covering what the solution does, who it is for, and how to start.
  • Gather user feedback and return it to the AI Center of Excellence and the crew team to improve agent and workflow design.
  • Support the clean transition of successful pilots into their permanent organizational home, with documented handoff.

5. Change Management & Communications

  • Apply a change approach proportionate to the size of each change: impact assessment, sponsor engagement, attention to concerns, and reinforcement after launch.
  • Work with HR and Research leaders when AI adoption affects roles, responsibilities, or ways of working. HR owns workforce decisions.
  • Coordinate with BM&SP communications and Research leadership so AI updates arrive as a coherent story, not a stream of separate announcements.
  • Maintain a single, easy-to-find home for Research AI guidance, examples, and upcoming sessions, for example a SharePoint site.

6. Measurement & Reporting

  • Track adoption breadth (who is using), depth (how often and for which use cases), and workflow adoption. Add short pulse surveys and colleague stories.
  • Assess whether the materials and sessions work: completion, feedback, and change in use. Use the findings to improve the next wave.
  • Report monthly to the VP and quarterly to the Research Leadership Team, with recommendations on where to invest, adjust, or stop.
  • Retire or revise approaches that are not driving adoption.

7. Partnerships

  • AI Center of Excellence: agree a working model for how adoption needs, agent releases, and policy updates flow between teams.
  • BM&SP crew team: stay close to active experiments so adoption planning starts before solutions are ready.
  • HR, Research communications, Technology & Operations, and Legal: engage as needed, and reuse existing training and change resources before building new ones.

Required Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in technology adoption, change management, internal training, learning design, or enablement in a large, matrixed organization.
  • Demonstrated change management experience: a track record of shifting behavior and ways of working across large, varied groups.
  • Hands-on experience designing and developing learning content in multiple formats (written guides, recorded video, e-learning), including defining learning objectives, piloting, and improving from feedback.
  • Hands-on fluency with Copilot, Claude, or similar generative AI tools, and the ability to show practical use credibly to non-technical colleagues.
  • Skill at designing simple, role-based adoption plans and materials that colleagues use, rather than full curricula.
  • Experience delivering engaging live and virtual training to varied audiences.
  • Strong prioritization judgment: able to focus limited capacity on the segments and use cases with the most impact.
  • Ability to influence and align leaders, managers, and technical partners without direct authority.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication in plain, direct language, with the ability to make complex or technical subjects simple.
  • Comfort working with usage data and simple adoption and training measures, such as attendance, completion, and feedback.
  • Flexibility and adaptability: comfort in a role that will evolve as the organization and the transformation evolve, and the judgment to adjust priorities as they change.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A qualification in training, teaching, or learning design, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience with a learning management system and with building SharePoint pages or similar guidance sites.
  • Experience designing accessible learning content for varied learning styles.
  • Experience in research publishing, scholarly communication, or information services.
  • Experience supporting adoption of AI agents, workflow automation, or similar process change.
  • Experience building and running champion or peer-network programs.
  • Familiarity with Wiley or similar globally distributed organizations.
  • Formal change management training or certification.

ABOUT GREYSTAR


Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. Headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina, Greystar manages and operates over $350 billion of real estate in more than 260 markets globally with offices throughout North America, Europe, South America, and the Asia-Pacific region. Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit .

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

The Development Accountant will be responsible for all accounting duties for their project portfolio. The position will be part of our Central Region accounting team, collaborating to achieve department and company-wide goals. This position should have the ability to work individually and, in a team setting.

JOB DESCRIPTION

  • Financial Accounting – Applies generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) to compile and analyze financial information into various financial statements and accounting reports. Makes appropriate journal entries in the general ledger by checking calculations, reviewing basis for figures, and balancing and reconciling figures.
  • Cost Accounting & Budget Management – Maintains development and construction budgets for all aspects of the project life cycle. Completes various forecasting and analysis to ensure accuracy and completeness of job cost reports. Assists development and construction directors to effectively manage project budgets.
  • Project Abstracts – Develops a general understanding of the underlying agreements and investment materials for assigned projects. Works to become familiar with the specific sections that are relevant to better understand the overall structure, including commitments, cost classifications, JV and lender requirements, and project fees.
  • Customer Relationships - Establish and maintains professional communication with all internal and external project stakeholders. Ensures customer satisfaction by responding to various requests from external investors, lenders, and others related to financial reports, project and construction draws.
  • Cash Management – Accurately and timely manages all assigned cash accounts. Performs monthly bank reconciliations, wire transfers, deposits, and other payment processes to ensure vendors are paid in a timely manner. Effectively works with development and construction teams to accurately forecast cash needs.
  • Collaboration – Establishes and maintains professional communication with all internal and external project stakeholders. Develops good working relationships with other departments including but not limited to; Accounts Payable, Finance, Asset Management, Property Management, Development and Construction.
  • Annual Audits - Acts as liaison to internal and external auditors by explaining journal entries and financial transactions. Provides research data and information as requested and answering questions necessary to complete the audit in a timely manner.

Qualifications


  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting
  • 1 - 2+ years of professional accounting experience; construction or real estate development experience preferred
  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel
  • Strong attention to detail with creative problem-solving skills
  • Excellent interpersonal and relationship-management skills, with the ability to establish, cultivate, and maintain relationships across internal and external stakeholders
  • Demonstrated ability to think critically and work independently, exercising sound judgment to drive tasks forward with minimal oversight

The salary range for this position is $70,000 - $78,000.


Additional Compensation:


Many factors go into determining employee pay within the posted range including business requirements, prior experience, current skills and geographical location.

  • Corporate Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in a quarterly or annual bonus program based on individual and company performance.
  • Onsite Property Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in weekly, monthly, and/or quarterly bonus programs.

Robust Benefits Offered*:

  • Competitive Medical, Dental, Vision, and Disability & Life insurance benefits. Low (free basic) employee Medical costs for employee-only coverage.
  • Generous Paid Time off. All new hires start with 15 days of vacation, 4 personal days, 10 sick days, and 11 paid holidays. Plus your birthday off after 1 year of service! Additional vacation accrued with tenure.
  • For onsite team members, onsite housing discount at Greystar-managed communities are available subject to discount and unit availability.
  • 6-Week Paid Sabbatical after 10 years of service (and every 5 years thereafter).
  • 401(k) with Company Match up to 6% of pay after 6 months of service.
  • Paid Parental Leave and lifetime Fertility Benefit reimbursement up to $10,000 (includes adoption or surrogacy).
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Critical Illness, Accident, Hospital Indemnity, Pet Insurance and Legal Plans.
  • Charitable giving program and benefits.

*Benefits offered for full-time employees. For Union and Prevailing Wage roles, compensation and benefits may vary from the listed information above due to Collective Bargaining Agreements and/or local governing authority.

This position may be performed remotely anywhere within the United States except the state of Alaska.

Job Description— Senior Accountant

Reports to:Corporate Controller

Pay Range DOE: 80,000 - 100,000 CAD

About Arc Beverage

Arc Beverage provides beverage co-manufacturing, packaging, and related operational services for brand owners. Our finance team partners with operations to maintain accurate financial records, support business decisions, and improve accounting processes.

Location and working hours

This position is based in Canada. Candidates must reside in Canada and be legally authorized to work in Canada. Regular working hours must align with Pacific Time (PT), including Pacific Standard Time (PST) and Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), as applicable. Additional availability may be needed during month-end and year-end close.

About the role

The Senior Accountant / Assistant Controller is a hands-on finance professional responsible for leading the accounting close, maintaining reliable financial reporting, and overseeing cost and inventory accounting. This role supports the Controller, reviews transactional accounting work, and partners with operations to explain financial results and strengthen controls.

Key responsibilities

  • Support the Controller in managing the day-to-day accounting and financial reporting functions.
  • Own and coordinate key components of the monthly, quarterly, and annual close processes.
  • Prepare and review journal entries, accruals, prepayments, amortization, reclassifications, and other accounting adjustments.
  • Prepare, review, and maintain detailed balance sheet reconciliations and supporting schedules.
  • Investigate and resolve accounting discrepancies, unusual transactions, and reconciliation issues.
  • Prepare monthly financial statements and management reporting packages.
  • Analyze financial results and investigate significant variances against budget, forecast, and prior periods.
  • Perform and review bank, credit card, accounts receivable, accounts payable, and other account reconciliations.
  • Support oversight of the accounts payable and accounts receivable functions, including vendor and customer account issues.
  • Maintain and review fixed asset, prepaid expense, accrual, lease, and other balance sheet accounts.
  • Support inventory accounting, including inventory reconciliations, costing, COGS, adjustments, and investigation of variances.
  • Review capital expenditures and ensure appropriate capitalization and accounting treatment.
  • Assist with cash management, cash flow reporting, and working capital analysis.
  • Ensure accounting transactions are properly recorded, supported, and classified in accordance with applicable accounting standards and company policies.
  • Support technical accounting assessments for new or unusual transactions.
  • Assist with annual audits, tax filings, and other external reporting requirements.
  • Prepare audit schedules and respond to auditor requests.
  • Maintain and strengthen internal controls, accounting policies, and procedures.
  • Identify process inefficiencies and implement improvements to increase accuracy, efficiency, and scalability.

As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.



About the Role:

CrowdStrike is looking for a highly motivated, self-driven Engagement Lead to oversee forensic investigations performed by CrowdStrike’s trusted partners. This Engagement Lead will be dedicated to making a difference in global security by protecting organizations against a wide range of attackers. This person will coordinate directly with both CrowdStrike’s incident response leadership and the leadership of our partners and customers, representing CrowdStrike and helping deliver high-quality results during high-stakes incident response investigations.

Am I a Partner Services Engagement Lead candidate?

  • Have you led teams through complicated incident response investigations?
  • Have you managed and built trust with teams of incident responders?
  • Are you comfortable with communicating about technical incident response findings to customer leadership, especially during high-pressure situations?
  • Do you find yourself interested in and keeping up with the latest vulnerabilities and breaches?
  • Are you self-motivated and looking for an opportunity to rapidly accelerate your skills?
  • Do you have an Incident Response or Information Security background that you’re not fully utilizing?
  • Are you a mentor who can naturally teach your colleagues new methods and approaches?
  • Do you love working around like-minded, smart people who you can learn from on a daily basis?

  • Support partners in effectively communicating with executives on the topics of forensics and malware analysis
  • Help train partners on new methods to hunt for bad actors across large sets of data
  • Effectively coordinate under the direction of outside counsel
  • Coach and mentor partners on advanced methods of performing host and/or network-based forensics across Windows, Mac, and Linux platforms
  • Help review and provide strategic, applicable, and feasible recommendations to help mature the security posture of organizations during and after an incident
  • Review written and verbal reports, presentations, recommendations, and findings for key stakeholders, including customer management, regulators, and legal counsel, to ensure alignment with CrowdStrike quality standards
  • Supervise current projects and coordinate all team members to keep workflow on track
  • Plan internal process improvement initiatives and facilitate execution by cross-functional teams
  • Maintain and update templates and internal process documentation

What You'll Need:

Successful candidates will have experience in one or more of the following areas:

  • Team leadership experience in a matrixed consulting environment
  • Previous experience developing and managing relationships in a consulting environment, preferably involving incident response
  • Incident Response: experience conducting or managing incident response investigations for organizations, investigating targeted threats such as the Ransomware, eCrime, Business Email Compromises (BECs)
  • Experience in project management, from conception to delivery
  • Experience managing external resources
  • Experience implementing technology projects
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
  • Demonstrate self-learning capabilities, taking initiative in a fast pace/quickly changing environment
  • Good communication and interpersonal skills capable of maintaining strong relationships
  • Strong organizational and multi-tasking skills
  • Excellent analytical and problem solving abilities
  • Team-management and leadership skills with cross-functional groups across divisions, worldwide, as part of a team
  • Documentation management and ability to use project management tools
  • Attention to details even under pressure
  • Time management skills with the ability to meet deadlines
  • Liaising with project stakeholders concerning project details and deliverables
  • Experience with identifying and implementing process efficiencies and monitoring the efficacy of updated workflows
  • Comfort with proactively and independently driving for results in small team environments
  • Experience working for consulting organizations
  • Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Additionally, all candidates must possess the following qualifications:

  • Capable of reviewing technical investigation results for accuracy, consistency, and completeness
  • Desire to grow and expand both technical and soft skills
  • Strong project management skills
  • Contributing thought leader within the incident response industry
  • Ability to foster a positive work environment and attitude
  • Ability to travel on short notice, up to 30% of the time

  • Comprehensive physical and mental wellness programs
  • Competitive vacation and holidays for recharge

  • Professional development opportunities for all employees regardless of level or role

raw.title: Wiz Customer Engineer
raw.excerpt: As the Wiz Customer Engineer at Foresite, you own everything pre-sales Wiz.
raw.description:
As the Wiz Customer Engineer at Foresite, you own everything pre-sales Wiz. If a customer is interested in Wiz and hasn't bought a license yet, you are the person who gets them to a confident yes. You'll run proofs of value, workshops, and CTFs, show customers things about their cloud environment that they didn't know, leveraging the power of Foresite services, and carry those wins through to implementation and managed services. You'll work side by side with Foresite’s Business Development team, and you'll be the go-to Wiz expert on Foresite's Customer Engineering team. If you know the full Wiz platform inside and out, love putting it in front of customers, and want to be close to the deals you help win, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

  • Own Pre-Sales Wiz:Be the single owner of Foresite's pre-sales Wiz motion, including proofs of value (POVs), workshops, and capture-the-flag (CTF) events, from first conversation to readout.

  • Run POVs End to End:Scope, launch, and deliver Wiz POVs, configuring the platform, guiding customers through connectors and onboarding, and presenting findings that show clear, prioritized risk in the customer's own environment.

  • Demonstrate the Full Wiz Platform:Position and demo Wiz Cloud, Wiz Code, Wiz Defend, and Wiz One together, showing how code, cloud, and runtime context connect to reduce risk across the full lifecycle.

  • Deliver Fast Time to Value:Surface meaningful, customer-specific findings within the first days of an engagement, and turn them into the business case for purchase.

  • Partner With Google Cloud Security / Wiz:Work directly with Google / Wiz sellers and Google / Wiz sales engineers to qualify opportunities, plan POVs, and win deals together. Take part in Google / Wiz partner programs and POV enablement, including shadowed engagements early on and independent delivery afterward.

  • Work Alongside Foresite Sellers:Partner with Foresite account executives and the rest of Customer Engineering to identify and qualify opportunities, understand technical and compliance objections, and resolve blockers.

  • Move Fast:Launch POVs quickly under a streamlined SOW, so customers can start when they are ready.

  • Convert Wins to Production:Hand successful POVs to Foresite's delivery and managed services teams, and help scope the implementation, ongoing management, and expansion that follow.

  • Write and Price the Work:Author SOWs and support pricing and commercials for Wiz engagements.

  • Shape Managed Services:Share what you see in the field about where Wiz managed services fit best, and help Foresite refine its offerings with Wiz.

  • Grow Across the Portfolio:Build working knowledge of Google SecOps and Google Unified Security over time, so you can support broader opportunities as needed.

  • Be a Thought Leader:Keep up with Wiz releases and cloud security trends, and contribute to best practices and thought leadership within Foresite.

Who You Are

  • 3+ years of experience in a customer-facing cloud security role, such as sales engineer, solutions architect, security consultant, or professional services. Hands-on, production experience with the Wiz platform across multiple products, including Wiz Cloud, Wiz Code, Wiz Defend, and Wiz One. Cloud-only experience is not enough.

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

  • Highly certified across the Wiz portfolio, with a commitment to keeping certifications current.

  • Experience running POVs, pilots, or customer evaluations of cloud security platforms, from kickoff through readout.

  • Experience in cloud security: CSPM, CWPP, CNAPP, cloud detection and response, and identity and access management, across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

  • Strong understanding of security principles and technologies, including vulnerability management, container and Kubernetes security, infrastructure as code, and application security in the software lifecycle.

  • Demonstrated ability to thrive in a fast-moving environment, with a strong willingness to learn new technologies and work positively with internal teams, partners, and customers.

  • Ability to work cross-functionally with sellers, project managers, security engineers, delivery teams, and partners.

  • Expert proficiency in using AI systems to accelerate productivity.

  • Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, including the ability to lead technical workshops and demos.

  • Experience writing technical documentation, including SOWs.

  • Experience in pricing and commercials.

  • Impeccable attention to detail.

  • Ability to travel up to 30% of the time as required

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience at Wiz, whether in pre-sales, post-sales, or customer success, or deep experience at a Wiz partner or customer.

  • Experience running Wiz CTFs, workshops, or other customer enablement events.

  • Experience with Google Cloud Security products, especially Security Command Center (SCC), Google SecOps SIEM and SOAR, Google Threat Intelligence, and Google Unified Security.

  • Experience with managed security services, and the ability to connect a POV to a managed service offering.

  • Experience with AI security solutions (Model Armor, etc.) and AI workload security in the cloud.

  • Experience developing clear architecture diagrams that show system layout, data flow, and connectivity.

  • Experience in any of these market sectors: retail, healthcare, energy, or chemicals.

  • Knowledge of cybersecurity market trends (e.g., ransomware, attack frameworks, zero trust, cloud-native threats).

Why Join Foresite?

At Foresite, we aren’t just another security provider—we are a mission-driven partner helping organizations navigate an increasingly complex threat landscape. We’ve built a global leader in SecOps and MDR by leaning into three core pillars that set us apart from the crowd:

  • The "Google Bet" Has Paid Off: Four years ago, we took a contrarian path by going all-in on Google Cloud. Today, that strategy is validated. As a Google Cloud Security Partner of the Year, we operate at the absolute cutting edge of the industry, offering our team a front-row seat to the future of security operations.

  • Practitioner Credibility: We were founded by security practitioners, and more importantly, we are still governed by them. We speak the language of the SOC because we’ve lived it. This ensures our strategy is driven by technical reality, not just marketing trends.

  • Room to Run: We are at that "sweet spot" of growth—large enough to win global contracts, but early enough that every individual’s contribution directly shapes our trajectory.

Position Description & Overview:

The Girard School of Business at Merrimack College has openings for an Undergraduate
course for Foundations of Applied AI for the Spring 2027 semester.

Undergraduate course:

Foundations of Applied AI (BAI1000)

Online Asynchronous

The course starts on January 13th and will run through May 7th, 2027.

Course descriptions:

Foundations of Applied AI (BAI1000):

This course introduces students from all disciplines to the rapidly expanding field of artificial intelligence (AI). It focuses on developing AI literacy through technical proficiency, practical application, and critical evaluation. At first, students develop a clear understanding of machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), large language models (LLMs), GenAI, and agentic AI techniques. Next, they actively learn about their unique practical applications in prompting and augmented workflows for individuals and organizations. Lastly, they assess and critique the validity, fairness, and ethical dimensions of the outputs of these AI systems. In this way, the students develop a personal AI portfolio of solutions to the problems in their fields of study by partnering with AI algorithms. No prior AI experience is required. Formerly titled Introduction to Artificial Intelligence.

This course is fully online and asynchronous. Applicants should be comfortable creating and recording video content for use within the course.

Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in business or related area, Ph.D. preferred. College teaching experience is preferred, although related work experience may be considered.

Application Materials Should Include:

  • Cover letter (with availability) stating motivation and interest in the position, citing experience relevant to the qualifications and including experience with, and commitment to, our Catholic Augustinian mission and our values.

  • Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV).

  • Syllabi (if applicable)

  • Teaching evaluations (past two years only).

This position is subject to the successful completion of a criminal background check.

Compensation

Minimum: $5,000 per 4-credit course

Minimum: $3,750 per lab section

The actual pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as, but not limited to, candidate qualifications and prior experience, scope of responsibilities, internal equity, and market considerations.

Statement on Our Mission

Merrimack College is a Catholic Augustinian institution of higher education committed to building an accepting and respectful community. Our mission is to enlighten minds, engage hearts and empower lives and is inspired by our Catholic faith and the Augustinian tradition of seeking truth through inquiry and dialogue.

Merrimack College seeks candidates who understand, respect, and can contribute to Merrimack’s Catholic and Augustinian mission. All candidates should describe in their application how they will foster a culture that supports our mission.

About Merrimack College

The only Catholic, Augustinian institution of higher education in New England, Merrimack College is a private, independent, coeducational institution with more than 4,000 undergraduate and 1,900 graduate students from 46 states and 45 countries. The College features more than 160 career-focused academic programs in science, engineering, business, nursing, health sciences, education, social sciences and humanities across undergraduate, professional and graduate programs, all taught by exceptional faculty who are passionate about their subject and student success. The College has six schools: arts and sciences, engineering and computational sciences, nursing and health sciences, education and social policy, the Girard school of business, and the Graduate School of counseling and social work. The College’s suburban 220-acre campus is just north of Boston in North Andover, Massachusetts. Merrimack is a Master’s Colleges and Universities/Larger Programs (M1) institution in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. Merrimack is one of the fastest-growing educational institutions in the country and has steadily climbed up in the U.S. News & World Report’s ranking of Best Colleges, ranking 37th in the Regional Universities North category in 2025. Merrimack is a NCAA Division I athletic institution.

Merrimack College is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

As part of the Corporate Traveler family - one of FCTG’s most successful global brands, we also benefit from a world-class support network and decades of experience in simplifying business travel.   • Une connaissance de TRACES NT et/ou de CargoWise.

  • Une connaissance de la réglementation européenne relative aux importations et à la sécurité alimentaire.

  • Une expérience dans le traitement documentaire de produits de la pêche, alimentaires ou agricoles.

  • La maîtrise du français et/ou de l’arabe.

Ready to innovate, collaborate, and make a difference? Join us and bring your big ideas to life while working in a dynamic, flexible environment that fuels your creativity and drive.

Our headquarters is in Lexington, Massachusetts, an inspiring healthcare research hub in a historic town.

Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit:

raw.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint is hiring a Junior Help Desk Specialist to provide first-contact support for authorized users of the Defense Casualty Information Processing System (DCIPS) Future. You will troubleshoot common issues, document requests, and refer unresolved problems to the appropriate team. The work calls for accurate records, discretion, and courteous service in a sensitive Department of Defense mission.

You will work from established procedures with guidance from experienced specialists and service-desk leads. Under Total Contact Ownership, you will keep users informed and track assigned requests through resolution, including when another team handles the technical work.

This position is fully remote. The DCIPS Future user-support service window is 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, excluding government holidays. Individual work schedules are assigned to support that coverage.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Receive incidents, service requests, and inquiries through approved support channels. Record, categorize, and prioritize each contact in the service-management system.
  • Troubleshoot DCIPS Future application use, user access, and related software, hardware, and connectivity issues using standard operating procedures and knowledge articles.
  • Verify user identity and support account creation, changes, deactivation, and credential maintenance under approved security procedures. Perform account actions within assigned permissions and route other actions to authorized administrators. Follow approved least-privilege procedures consistent with Zero Trust principles.
  • Document symptoms, affected users, troubleshooting steps, and results. Escalate unresolved issues to Tier 2, Tier 3, or the responsible technical team with a clear record of work completed.
  • Track assigned tickets after escalation, communicate status and next steps, confirm the outcome with users, and record resolution and closure.
  • Recognize possible outages or security incidents and promptly notify the designated lead or response team.
  • Coordinate DCIPS-related hardware exchange, repair-service requests, and other support dependencies with the responsible service providers.
  • Identify recurring questions and gaps in documentation. Help update self-service guidance and troubleshooting articles, and provide feedback on user training.
  • Maintain accurate service-performance data and handover notes, including open actions and escalation status.
  • Protect controlled unclassified information and sensitive personal and mission data using approved tools and handling procedures.
  • Complete DCIPS-specific training and practice support workflows, use of knowledge resources, and escalation procedures before service activation and as the application changes.

Qualifications

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Zero to two years of experience in technical support, a help desk, or customer service. Prior experience is not required.
  • Basic understanding of IT systems, networks, and security concepts, including Windows, Microsoft 365, and connectivity troubleshooting.
  • Familiarity with ticketing systems such as ServiceNow, Remedy, Jira Service Management, or comparable tools.
  • Awareness of Active Directory, multi-factor authentication, VPNs, and remote access, and an understanding of ITIL-based incident and service-request processes.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, careful documentation, and the ability to assist users with varying technical backgrounds.
  • Ability to follow procedures, manage competing requests calmly, and develop technical skills through training.

Preferred certifications

  • CompTIA Security+
  • CompTIA A+ or Network+
  • ITIL 4 Foundation

However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.

This is a remote position.

Part-Time Human Resources Business Partner (Fractional / Contract)

Employment Type:Part-Time, Contract, Remote within the U.S.

Location:Remote (U.S.-based)

Hours:Up to 60 hours per month (about 15 hours per week)
Compensation:$55 to $65 per hour, commensurate with experience

About Cause Capacity

Cause Capacity partners with nonprofits and small businesses to strengthen their people, systems, and operations. We step in as embedded partners—helping organizations run more effectively so they can focus on their mission and growth.

Our clients are often in moments of transition or expansion. They don’t just need extra hands—they need thoughtful, reliable partners who can bring structure, clarity, and follow-through. Learn more ator check us out onLinkedIn.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced,client-focusedHuman Resources Business Partner to provide high-quality HR support to our nonprofit and small business clients.

You’ll partner with clients and the Cause Capacity team on a wide range of people operations, including HR policy, employee relations, compliance, payroll, recruiting, and workplace investigations. You’ll serve as atrusted advisor, bringing sound judgment and employment law expertise to help clients handle everything from everyday HR needs to complex people matters.

This role is ideal for someone looking for a remote,part-timeHR position in the nonprofit, mission-driven space who wants to make an impact by helping mission-driven organizations and growing businesses build strong people practices.

Who You Are

You’re the seasoned HR professional clients turn to for clear guidance and a steady hand. You bring deep expertise, exercise sound judgment, and take a thoughtful, client-focused approach to supporting mission-driven organizations and growing companies.

You might describe yourself as:

Trusted- You build credibility quickly, offer clear and practical guidance, and handle confidential matters with discretion.

Knowledgeable- You have in-depth knowledge of HR best practices and employment laws in various states.

Analytical- You bring strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills to analyze complex situations and recommend practical solutions.

Adaptable- You can shift easily between clients and priorities and stay organized in a remote work environment.

Detail-oriented- You have a keen eye for detail and are committed to maintaining accuracy and consistency in your work.

What You’ll Do

The Human Resources Business Partner will operate as an independent contractor and part of the Cause Capacity team to deliver seamless, high-quality human resources support to our clients. Key responsibilities may include:

HR Policy

  • Research best practices to inform the development and revision of HR policies and procedures.

  • Develop, write, and update HR policies, employee handbooks, and standard operating procedures.

  • Partner with the Human Resources Associate on policy implementation and client questions.

Employee Relations

  • Provide guidance on plans for continuous employee development.

  • Develop and administer performance improvement plans.

Compliance

  • Develop and deliver virtual employee training programs and maintain related documentation.

  • Manage annual sexual harassment prevention training for clients.

Payroll and Benefits

  • Administer HRIS and payroll systems and troubleshoot issues as needed.

  • Manage client payroll, including processing payroll, conducting payroll audits, pulling reports, and investigating and resolving employee issues.

  • Initiate and process employee pay changes and ensure updates are accurately reflected in payroll and HRIS systems.

  • Work with clients on benefits offerings and annual open enrollment.

Onboarding

  • Develop and refine onboarding processes, advise clients on their roles, and recommend best practices.

  • Initiate pre-onboarding actions and oversee onboarding across multiple clients, including background checks, offer letters, new-hire correspondence, and processing actions into payroll and HRIS systems.

  • Audit and verify completion of the onboarding process.

  • Coordinate the administration, development, and scheduling of new-employee onboarding programs.

Offboarding and Terminations

  • Develop and refine offboarding processes.

  • Coordinate and carry out employee offboarding.

  • Determine final payroll needs and process in accordance with applicable state payroll laws.

  • Document reasons for offboarding and termination.

Recruiting

  • Manage full-cycle recruiting, including intake calls, posting jobs to paid job sites, updating the applicant tracking system, scheduling and conducting phone interviews, writing interview questions, communicating with hiring managers and candidates, and checking references.

  • Draft job descriptions and benchmark salaries.

Investigations

  • Conduct prompt, thorough, and neutral workplace investigations regarding sexual harassment, age discrimination, or other protected areas covered by federal or applicable state law.

Other

  • Support project management needs of the team and help keep client deliverables, timelines, and priorities on track.

  • Contribute to special projects and other related work as needed.

What You Bring

Experience

  • 10-15 years of experience as an HR Manager, HR Generalist, or HR Business Partner

  • Strong employment law and compliance background

  • Current or recent experience applying California employment laws

  • Hands-on payroll processing experience

  • Current HR certification a plus

  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree preferred

  • Comfortable working in a remote, fast-moving, and client-facing environment and managing multiple priorities independently

Core Skills

  • Strong client and customer service aptitude

  • High attention to detail

  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills

  • Sound judgment and ability to maintain confidentiality

  • Ability to organize and prioritize workload, especially in a remote work environment

Technical Skills

  • Proficiency in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office

  • Proficiency in HRIS and payroll systems (e.g., Gusto, BambooHR)

  • Proficiency with applicant tracking tools

  • Familiarity with project management tools (e.g., Asana, Monday.com)

How This Role Works

  • This is a1099 contractor role, not a full-time position.

  • Hours are up to 40 per month and may vary month-to-month depending on client needs.

  • You’ll work both independently and as part of the Cause Capacity team.

  • You’ll support a variety of organizations, with responsibilities and priorities shaped by each client’s needs.

Why Join Cause Capacity

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Work from anywhere in the United States

  • Opportunity to do meaningful work that drives real impact for our clients

  • Work with a range of nonprofits and small businesses, each with unique people operations needs

How to Apply

We’d love to learn more about you! Complete the application found at.Please complete the pre-screening questions and submit your resume, along with a cover letter sharing your interest in this opportunity. Be sure to include all requested materials, as incomplete applications will not be considered.

Cause Capacity is an equal opportunity employer, and we value having a diverse team. We believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make us stronger and better able to serve our clients, and we encourage people from all backgrounds to apply. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The Program Event Manager is responsible for the overall project management, coordination, and successful execution of assigned event programs from initial planning through post-event completion. This position serves as the primary project manager for assigned event programs, ensuring that program delivery, speaker coordination, sponsor commitments, internal deliverables, and event timelines are effectively managed.

The Event Manager works cross-functionally with Event Directors, event logistics, marketing, sales, registration, design and other internal stakeholders to deliver high-quality events that align with organizational objectives, client expectations, and established standards.

This role requires strong project management skills, exceptional organization, proactive communication, and the ability to independently manage multiple projects and events with competing priorities.

Essential Duties:

  • Serve as the primary project manager for assigned events, overseeing program planning, development, coordination, and execution from kickoff through post-event completion.
  • Manage multiple event programs simultaneously, developing and maintaining project timelines, tracking milestones, and ensuring deadlines and deliverables are met.
  • Lead event planning meetings, coordinate project updates, and communicate responsibilities and expectations to stakeholders.
  • Proactively identify challenges, manage competing priorities, resolve issues, and escalate concerns when necessary.
  • Maintain accurate event information, speaker details, and program documentation in Salesforce and other event management systems.
  • Ensure compliance with established event management processes, procedures, and organizational standards.
  • Partner with Event Directors to develop and execute event agendas, session content, and program schedules.
  • Coordinate all aspects of speaker participation, including invitations, confirmations, communications, session assignments, and preparation.
  • Organize and facilitate speaker preparation calls, content meetings, and other program-related discussions.
  • Track speaker deliverables, session details, and presentation materials to ensure program readiness.
  • Collaborate with Event Directors and sales to coordinate sponsor speaking opportunities and contractual program commitments.
  • Ensure agenda and speaker information is accurate and consistent across event websites, internal systems, and event materials.
  • Serve as the central point of coordination between Event Directors, sales, marketing, logistics, design, and other internal departments throughout the event planning process.
  • Communicate project timelines, responsibilities, program requirements, and updates to ensure alignment across teams.
  • Build and maintain professional relationships with government officials, education leaders, industry executives, speakers, sponsors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Coordinate with marketing and design teams to ensure event materials, presentations, program guides, and signage are accurate and completed on schedule.
  • Partner with Event Logistics Managers to communicate program requirements, speaker needs, and onsite execution details.
  • Oversee onsite program execution, including speaker coordination, session management, presentation readiness, and agenda adjustments.
  • Ensure speakers, moderators, and program participants are prepared and supported throughout the event.
  • Collaborate with onsite teams to address challenges and ensure a seamless event experience for attendees, speakers, and sponsors.
  • Complete post-event follow-up, program documentation, and assigned closeout responsibilities.
  • Identify opportunities to improve event management workflows, communication, and operational efficiency.
  • Contribute to the development and refinement of event procedures, templates, timelines, and best practices.
  • Support the adoption and effective use of event management systems and emerging technologies.
  • Share lessons learned and recommendations to improve future event planning and execution.

§Job will require travel. Traveling on weekends may be necessary.

§Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple event programs, priorities, and deadlines simultaneously.

§Exceptional attention to detail and ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

§Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate professionally with high-level executives, government officials, and industry leaders.

§Strong problem-solving skills with a proactive, solutions-oriented approach.

§Ability to work independently, take initiative, and exercise sound judgment.

§Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to build and maintain positive relationships across teams and with external stakeholders.

§Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, PowerPoint, Salesforce, and other event and project management platforms.

§Familiarity with AI-powered tools and emerging technologies, with a willingness to learn and leverage AI to streamline workflows, improve efficiency, and enhance event planning processes.

§Ability to adapt to changing priorities, processes, and technologies.

§Experience working in a remote or collaborative virtual environment preferred.

§Position requires travel, including occasional weekend travel.

§Must reside in and be authorized to work in the United States.

§Must maintain a professional remote work environment with reliable internet access.

Apply identity verification and access-control procedures; route actions outside assigned permissions to authorized administrators. Apply Zero Trust principles when troubleshooting authentication and access issues.
  • Prepare escalations with affected users, mission impact, diagnostic evidence, troubleshooting results, and the assistance required from Tier 2, Tier 3, or another technical team.
  • Track progress after escalation, communicate status and next steps, and verify and document the resolution with the user.
  • Identify emerging outages and suspected security incidents. Coordinate notifications with the Shift Lead and designated technical owners.

  • Review recurring issues and recommend improvements to support procedures, knowledge articles, and user training. Validate proposed self-service content using approved test environments and sample or sanitized data before submitting it for publication review.

  • Record service metrics, flag tickets at risk of missing service targets, and provide complete handovers of open incidents and actions.
  • Protect sensitive support data. Take part in DCIPS-specific training and checks of support workflows, knowledge resources, and escalation routes.

Qualifications

  • At least five years of IT customer-support or service-desk experience, including at least two years in a federal or defense environment.

  • Proficiency in Windows and Linux troubleshooting, user account administration, and remote desktop tools.
  • Knowledge of network fundamentals, VPNs, Active Directory, multi-factor authentication, and public key infrastructure certificate management.
  • Experience troubleshooting email, collaboration tools, and endpoint-security applications, with an understanding of Zero Trust and secure access management.
  • Familiarity with the Risk Management Framework, DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides, and DoD cybersecurity requirements.
  • Strong problem-solving, documentation, and customer-service skills, with the ability to work independently and coordinate with remote technical teams.

Preferred certifications

raw.description:
Want to deliver tech with purpose, with people who care?

Join us in our mission to create solutions that help keep children safe online.

Who are we?

Headquartered in Perth, Australia, with offices around the world, Qoria is an ASX-listed global leader in child digital safety technology and services. We are a purpose-driven business operating under the Linewize brand in North America and Asia Pacific, the Smoothwall brand in the UK, the Qustodio brand in EMEA, and Qoria LK in Sri Lanka.

Our solutions are used by schools, school districts, and parental communities to protect children from harmful online content, identify students at risk based on their digital behaviours, and help teachers maintain focus and safe learning environments in the digital classroom. Today, 30,000 schools and 7 million parents rely on our solutions to help keep 25 million children safe across 180 countries worldwide.

What’s the opportunity:

Qustodio supports families with innovative tools and meaningful guidance for a healthy and safe digital experience. As our CRM Manager, you’ll make sure every parent experiences that value quickly and gets more from it over time. You’ll own our lifecycle program and CRM tooling from signup onward: driving parents to protect their child’s device, set up the parent app, and see protection in action, then keeping them engaged with timely, relevant, well-crafted communication.

You’ll step into an established, high-performing program with one clear goal: to keep improving it. By continuously testing, optimizing and exploring new opportunities, you’ll drive measurable gains in activation, engagement and conversion. Reporting to the VP of Product, you’ll work closely with Engineering, Data, Design, Customer Support and Marketing.

Here’s how you’ll do it:

  • Product activation and engagement

Own the onboarding experience that turns signups into active users, guiding parents from protecting a child’s device to seeing protection in action.

Use product data and user behavior to trigger messaging at the moments that matter, such as blocked content, screen time limits or new app installs.

As part of the Product team, drive adoption of new features and shape how they’re introduced to parents.

Build retention journeys that deepen product usage and show ongoing value beyond the first 30 days.

Work with Customer Support to keep the Help Center accurate and aligned with the product, so parents can set up and get value on their own.

  • CRM tooling and channels

Own Qustodio’s Braze instance: canvases, segmentation, triggers and data quality.

Work with Engineering to keep event tracking and product data flowing reliably into Braze.

Uphold email best practices across deliverability, accessibility, frequency and consent.

Orchestrate email, push and in-app messaging as one consistent experience, coordinating with Marketing, QA, Design and Localization.

Manage the CRM calendar across departments.

  • Testing, insights and growth

Continuously test and optimize to improve activation, engagement and conversion.

Identify new opportunities across segments, journeys, channels and Braze capabilities.

Report on lifecycle KPIs alongside product metrics and turn learnings into action.

Bring the voice of the customer into product decisions through surveys and Customer Support insights, and keep the Help Center aligned with lifecycle messaging.

What you will bring:

  • 3+ years in CRM or lifecycle marketing, ideally in a subscription app, consumer SaaS.
  • Hands-on experience with Braze or a comparable CRM platform, including canvases, segmentation and triggered messaging.
  • A product mindset: you think in user journeys, activation milestones and behavioral data, not just campaign sends.
  • Strong knowledge of email best practices, deliverability and privacy regulations such as GDPR.
  • A rigorous testing approach and strong analytical skills, with comfort working in dashboards and alongside data teams.
  • Clear, concise writing and the ability to communicate results and recommendations to stakeholders.
  • Ability to own an established program independently, ramp up quickly and manage multiple priorities.
  • Fluent in English.

Why choose Qustodio by Qoria?

In this role, you can expect:

  • Great Benefits
  • Enhanced holiday & family leave
  • Tech Allowance
    .... and much more

More importantly, you'll:

  • Support tech with purpose..

At Qustodio by Qoria, your work truly matters. With every customer interaction, you’ll be helping children stay safe online. It feels good to do good.

  • With people who care...

One of our values is ‘Care, Always’. Our Support Team lives and breathes that, every day. We also look after each other and help create a supportive environment for all.

  • Through work that you love...

Working in this role takes skill, energy and resilience. It can also be incredibly rewarding. Here, your efforts will be visible and you’ll love the impact you have.

  • And a career that you own...

A proven career path forward, with real opportunities to progress your career into other teams and departments within the company. Exposure to industry leading tech, developed in-house by an amazing engineering team. Regular company wide lunch and learn sessions

We'd love to hear from you. Please submit your application if you would like to be considered for this opportunity.
